Subject: Catalyst AI - Implementation Maestro: Autoscale & Burst Plan

Hi Jordan / Catalyst team,

Thanks again for choosing Redwood Dedicated. As discussed in the demo, we want to kick off the implementation phase and lock in pool sizing, autoscale and burst policies, and regional placement so the ops team can start provisioning. To keep momentum I sketched a lightweight plan below and attached a provisioning template you can fill out: Maestro_Provisioning_Template.xlsx (stub).

Top-level asks from us to you:
- Confirm primary region(s) for production traffic (we typically recommend pairing a US and EU region for DR).
- Target steady-state concurrent slots (RPS/requests per minute) and expected peak burst multiplier (x1.5, x2, etc.).
- Any hard constraints: network egress limits, private subnet-only access, or specific KMS/HSM requirements.

Proposed initial defaults (we can adjust after your sizing):
- Primary region: us-west-2 (can fallback to eu-west-1)
- Steady pool: 8 A100-sim nodes (supports ~200 concurrent short-chat sessions)
- Burst policy: allow additional 4 nodes for up to 30 minutes when 90th percentile latency > 250ms
- Canary rollout: 10% traffic to new model/config for 24 hours

Next steps & timeline:
1) You return the completed template by Tue 11/17.
2) Internal provisioning call 11/18 with infra & netops (30 min).
3) Canary window 11/24-11/25 then full cutover 11/30.

CCing Monica (CS lead) and Priyom (implementation PM) to own the handoff. Monica — can you confirm team availability for the 11/18 provisioning call?

Attachments: Maestro_Provisioning_Template.xlsx (xlx stub)

Best,

Subject: Re: Catalyst AI - Implementation Maestro: Autoscale & Burst Plan

Jordan — thanks for the quick replies and the expected concurrency numbers; that helps. Answers inline and a recommended config below.

Ben / Catalyst team, please see the proposed technical choices. If that aligns we'll schedule the short provisioning call and I will open SUP-2345 for the activation tasks.

Q1 (burst provisioning): we typically stage burst capacity as additional nodes in the same pool but flagged as "burst" (separate VM class, faster scale-up policy). This reduces cold-start cold-cache impacts because we keep one warm replica class reserved for bursts. For your profile (long-lived sessions + heavy bursts) I recommend:
- Steady pool: 10 compute nodes (A100-sim equivalence)
- Burst pool: +8 nodes with pre-warmed images; auto-attach when queue > 75% for more than 45s
- Warm standby: 2 smaller GPU nodes to ensure fast KV cache population for short spikes

Q2 (route-based canaries): yes — our routing supports route-scoped canaries. We'll create a routing rule so only /recommendations receives 10% of new model/config traffic for 24h. If metrics are green we expand to full-API.

Autoscale and SLA tradeoffs (proposed):
- Scale-up threshold: queue latency 95th > 200ms OR GPU util > 78% sustained for 30s
- Scale-down threshold: sustained util < 40% for 5m with cooldown window 10m
- Burst duration cap: 45 minutes per event, with a 2-hour cool-down between burst activations to avoid runaway costs
- Monitoring: token-level cost & latency dashboards pinned to the deal in HubSpot and shared Drive (link below).

Security / networking note: Catalyst requested private-subnet-only access and KMS integration — we will include a private VPC peering step in the provisioning checklist. Priyom — please ensure netops ticket created and include KMS details.

Attachments referenced: Maestro_autoscale-config.yaml (stub) and internal onboarding checklist in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1MaestroOnboard
Jira: SUP-2345 created for activation and network tasks.

Action items (owner, due):
- Jordan: return completed provisioning template (by 2026-11-16 EOD) — Jordan
- Priyom: open netops/KMS ticket and invite netops to 11/18 call — Priyom (by 11/17)
- Karthik: prepare node sizing rationale & pre-warm plan — Karthik (by 11/17)
- Monica: schedule provisioning call and share dial-in — Monica (by 11/17)

Thanks — I think this puts us on a safe cost/perf path for your workload.

Monica Patel
